title: BAR Mapping with Attributes
description: Maps device BARs with the right memory attributes: uncacheable for registers, write-combining for framebuffers. Wrong attributes cause corruption or terrible performance; the driver chooses per region. It is the foundation of all MMIO.

demo.title: Demo — BAR Mapping with Attributes

title: Write-Combining Buffers
description: Uses write-combining memory to burst streaming writes to devices. WC buffers collect writes into full cache-line bursts instead of trickling bytes. GPUs and framebuffers depend on it for throughput.

demo.title: Demo — Write-Combining Buffers

title: Uncacheable Register Access
description: Accesses device registers as uncacheable so every read hits the hardware. Cached register reads return stale values; UC guarantees freshness. Control registers are always UC.

demo.title: Demo — Uncacheable Register Access

title: Posted Write Semantics
description: Understands that MMIO writes are posted: they complete from the CPU's view before reaching the device. Ordering between writes is preserved, but completion is not; a read-back or non-posted write acts as a barrier. Drivers synchronize accordingly.

demo.title: Demo — Posted Write Semantics

title: Read-Modify-Write Safety
description: Performs read-modify-write on registers with locking or atomic sequences. Concurrent RMW from two threads corrupts bits; spinlocks or hardware atomics serialize them. It is the classic driver race.

demo.title: Demo — Read-Modify-Write Safety

title: Doorbell Registers
description: Rings doorbell registers to notify hardware of new work instead of polling. The driver writes descriptors to memory, then one MMIO write kicks the device. Batching doorbells amortizes the MMIO cost.

demo.title: Demo — Doorbell Registers

title: Cache Coherency with Devices
description: Keeps CPU caches coherent with DMA through snooping or explicit flushes. Coherent interconnects snoop automatically; non-coherent ones need manual cache maintenance. Getting it wrong corrupts data silently.

demo.title: Demo — Cache Coherency with Devices

title: Huge Pages for MMIO
description: Maps large MMIO regions with huge pages to cut TLB pressure. A 1 GB BAR needs 262k 4K TLB entries but one 1G page; fewer misses mean faster access. It matters for big apertures.
key_mechanisms: Map large BARs with huge pages

demo.title: Demo — Huge Pages for MMIO

title: Userspace I/O with UIO/VFIO
description: Exposes MMIO to userspace safely with UIO for simple devices and VFIO for IOMMU-isolated ones. Userspace drivers map BARs directly, bypassing kernel overhead; the IOMMU keeps DMA safe. DPDK and SPDK are built on this.

demo.title: Demo — Userspace I/O with UIO/VFIO

title: Register Shadowing
description: Keeps software shadows of write-only registers to allow read-modify-write. Some registers cannot be read back; the shadow tracks their last written value. It enables safe bit manipulation on write-only hardware.

demo.title: Demo — Register Shadowing

title: Memory Ordering Barriers
description: Places memory barriers to order MMIO against normal memory accesses. Weakly ordered architectures reorder freely; barriers enforce the sequence the hardware requires. Missing barriers cause Heisenbugs.

demo.title: Demo — Memory Ordering Barriers

title: MSI-X Tables in MMIO
description: Programs MSI-X vector tables that live in MMIO BARs. The driver writes message address and data per vector into the table; the device reads them to signal interrupts. It ties MMIO programming to interrupt delivery.

demo.title: Demo — MSI-X Tables in MMIO

title: Cache-Line Padding
description: Pads per-CPU MMIO-adjacent structures to cache lines to avoid false sharing. Two cores hammering adjacent words in one line ping-pong the cache; padding isolates them. It is cheap insurance for hot paths.

demo.title: Demo — Cache-Line Padding

title: Device Memory Fences
description: Uses device-specific fences to order operations within the device. Some accelerators need explicit fence commands between batches; the driver inserts them per the programming model. It is the device-side analog of CPU barriers.
key_mechanisms: Insert fences per the programming model

demo.title: Demo — Device Memory Fences

title: Write-Back Register Caching
description: Caches frequently-written registers in write-back software caches with flush on demand. For registers written far more than read, batching writes cuts MMIO traffic. Flush points are chosen where hardware needs consistency.

demo.title: Demo — Write-Back Register Caching
